title: Files and Games panels — open, close and switch

steps.path: In chat view, click Files in the header to open it, then click it again to close. Do the same with Games
steps.headline: Open and close Files, then Games. Does each panel glide in AND glide out, instead of popping?
steps.changed: The panel's left edge now glides open and shut while it fades, over about a quarter of a second. The chat re-wraps exactly once per action and never during the motion: it makes room first when a panel opens, and takes the room back last when it closes. While a panel leaves it keeps showing what it had; before, closing Files emptied it in the same instant.
steps.notice: A smooth glide both ways. When closing, the panel still shows your file as it goes. The chat text jumps to its new width once, at the start of an open or the end of a close, and holds still while the panel moves.
steps.risk: If you see a flash of the panel reappearing at the very end of a close, or the chat's one jump bothers you, say so in the note.

steps.path: With Files open, click Games. Then with Games open, click Files. Try it after dragging the Files panel wider or narrower
steps.headline: Switch between Files and Games, which are different widths. Does the panel glide to its new size instead of jumping?
steps.changed: Files and Games are different widths, and Files can be resized. Switching used to snap from one width to the other. Now the contents swap at once and the panel's edge glides to the new width. Going to the wider panel, the chat makes room first; going to the narrower one, the chat takes the spare room at the end.
steps.notice: The edge travels smoothly between the two widths, in both directions, and the new panel's contents are already the right size from the first frame, never stretched and then snapped.
steps.risk: For a moment while shrinking, a strip of plain background shows on the panel's left as the edge travels across it; say if that reads as a glitch.

steps.path: Click Files, and click it again before it has finished opening. Click rapidly. Click Files then Games in quick succession
steps.headline: Click again mid-motion, and click rapidly. Does the panel reverse smoothly from wherever it is, with no jump or restart?
steps.changed: Every step starts from wherever the panel visibly is at that moment, rather than from the beginning, so a second click turns the motion around instead of restarting it.
steps.notice: No snapping to fully open or fully shut before moving; no panel left half open; no empty gap left beside the chat after rapid clicking.
steps.risk: Rapid clicking is where a stuck panel or a leftover gap would show up. If you ever end up with blank space where a panel was, that is the bug to report.

steps.path: Leave a panel open. Switch to another tab and back. Press Ctrl+` to go to terminal view, open and close a panel there, and come back
steps.headline: With a panel open, switch tabs and flip views. Does it stay put, and does terminal view animate the same way?
steps.changed: The app rebuilds the panel whenever you switch tabs or flip between chat and terminal view. The animation is tied to the act of opening, closing or switching, so a panel that was already open is simply there. Terminal view now uses the same panel code as chat view, so it animates identically.
steps.notice: An already-open panel never wipes in a second time. In terminal view, open, close and switch all glide exactly as they do in chat view, and the frosted window frame around the panel stays lined up with it throughout.
steps.risk: The frame's cut-out and the panel are moved by the same value, but this is the area most likely to show a one-frame mismatch; say if the frame and the panel ever disagree.
